clue.text: Make unknown spirit

parts.note: a make is a brand, as in a make of car
Y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An instruction to conjure an unidentified ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' reads as a verb but is the noun, a manufacturer's label.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and spirits are strong distilled drinks.

clue.text: Hurry finding difficult situation in secret passage

parts.note: to bolt is to dash off quickly
being in a hole means being in trouble

explanation.surface: Rushing to escape a predicament through a hidden tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolthole is an escape route or hiding place.

clue.text: One unsuccessful in getting a place

definitions.text: One unsuccessful in getting a place

parts.words: One unsuccessful in getting a place
parts.note: describes a horse or competitor that did not finish among the leaders

explanation.surface: Describes someone who failed to secure a position.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, a place is a finish in the top few; others are listed as having merely run.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing idiom for a loser, someone who competed but failed to finish placed.

clue.text: Dope reads about one who is reckless

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug-taker reading up on a daredevil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DOPE READS.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, rash outlaw.

clue.text: Biretta symbolic of the working-class?

parts.note: a biretta is a priest's square cap; the clue playfully asks for the cap that stands for manual labourers, the flat woollen kind

explanation.surface: A clerical hat oddly standing for the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: A biretta is just a cap here; the British flat cap made of cloth is the traditional emblem of the working man.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat headgear of the British labourer is a woollen soft hat, so it is the working-class emblem.

clue.text: Most contemptible individual one cannot get beneath

explanation.surface: The worst person imaginable, beyond whom nothing lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the most despicable person, and literally the bottom-most, with nothing below.

clue.text: Not all of the pill was put on board

indicators.note: the pill's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

explanation.surface: Part of a pill was set down on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: To table a motion is to put it before a board.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a proposal is to present it formally at a meeting.

clue.text: Business going first?

parts.note: a thriving business is a going something; here the second word is wanted, with going said to come first

explanation.surface: Asks whether a firm comes before others.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'going concern' is a functioning business, so the answer follows 'going'.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a firm or commercial enterprise.

clue.text: Peter French

parts.note: reads as a person's full name but asks for the French form of the name Peter

explanation.surface: Seems to name a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like a surname but means 'in French'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre is the French equivalent of the given name Peter.

clue.text: Rechabite banner

explanation.surface: Seems to name a placard for a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: Rechabites were a biblical people who abstained from wine, and a temperance society took the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rechabite abstains from alcohol and wants it outlawed; a banner is literally one who bans.

clue.text: Unbearable part of the camel's load

definitions.text: Unbearable part of the camel's load

parts.words: Unbearable part of the camel's load
parts.note: alludes to the proverb about the final light addition that breaks the camel's back

explanation.surface: Describes the piece of a camel's burden it cannot carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says one more piece of a cereal stalk broke the camel's back; figuratively, the final provocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the final small burden that makes a situation intolerable.

clue.text: Game not finished by quarter during bout of overindulgence

indicators.note: the game's name stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: bingo is a numbers game played in halls
E, East, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone unable to finish a game falls into a spree of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: BINGO cut short by 'not finished' gives BING; 'by' sets E beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spell of excessive eating or drinking.

clue.text: Charles did not finish being upset in front of first historic castle

indicators.note: places the rearranged piece before the next letter
upset signals the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
the name Charles stops short of its last letter
the first letter of historic is taken

explanation.surface: A royal Charles left a historic castle unfinished and was distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not finish' drops the S of Charles, leaving CHARLE; 'being upset' rearranges that to HARLEC, set 'in front of' H. Harlech is a Welsh castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech is a medieval fortress in north Wales built by Edward I.

clue.text: Grizzly female maybe

parts.note: a grizzly is a kind of bear, and a female one is named with the pronoun prefix

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a grumpy or grey-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grizzly' suggests grizzled or complaining, but it is the North American bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A grizzly is a North American bear, and a female animal of that kind is a sow bear.

clue.text: In disarray Daniel loses point to the lady

indicators.note: disarray means the remaining letters are jumbled
the name Daniel gives up one letter

parts.note: E, East, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A man named Daniel in a muddle misses the point when speaking to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes E from DANIEL, leaving DANIL, which 'In disarray' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a particular woman.

clue.text: Flowering in said blue vase

indicators.note: said shows the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: taken as the colour word; a Ming is a prized Chinese porcelain vase from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Flowers arranged in what one calls a blue vase.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'blue Ming' runs together into a word for blossoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a plant in blossom, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Hurry up, Kate has me confused

indicators.note: confused shows the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone urging speed because Kate has muddled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges KATE HAS ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry up is to move quickly, an idiom for rushing.

clue.text: Surprised saying you and I will double up

indicators.note: the contraction is written twice in a row

parts.note: contracted, 'we will' becomes we'll

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that two people will pair off.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignoring the apostrophe, WE'LL is the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to express astonishment.

clue.text: Electrical device cooked her toast

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are fiddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's toast prepared by an electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges HER TOAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current.

clue.text: Worker with lad personally involved

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A labourer and a boy both directly engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on manager takes a direct practical part in the work.

clue.text: Deceitful fellow is a card

explanation.surface: A crooked man is also called a character.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, and also the old name for the jack in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Companion, old leader in navy struggling with fish

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the other
struggling suggests the letters thrash into a new order

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friend, a veteran captain, battles with a fish in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges NAVY to ANVY; CH and O (first of 'old') go 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchovy is a small salty sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: 150 are taking time with wine

indicators.note: the word are takes on, adds after it, the next piece

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people taking their time over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Yearn to have a turn but not recently

parts.note: to yearn is to long for something
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone eager for their go, though it was a while back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the distant past, the opposite of lately.

clue.text: Cancel article omitted from yearbook

indicators.note: the article is left out of the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone scrapping an item from the yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, so to revoke.

clue.text: In Lambeth I calculated it to be morally correct

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A calculation made in a London district is judged right.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth is a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct conforms to moral principles, so it is right and proper.

clue.text: Fall once more into evil ways with sticky outcome

definitions.text: Fall once more into evil ways

explanation.surface: Relapsing into wickedness leaves one in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SIN, the word means to sin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin again is to lapse back into wrongdoing; resin is the gummy substance that oozes from trees.

clue.text: Rock having even weight

parts.note: to iron is to smooth or even out
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A rock with a uniform mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to flatten creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron ore.

clue.text: Thin coated sheets can be found in front of shallow dish

indicators.note: places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a tin is a can, as for food
a plate is a flat shallow dish

explanation.surface: Thin sheets turning up before a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinplate is sheet steel thinly covered with a protective metal layer.

clue.text: Doctor Kay served jelly outside

indicators.note: the rearranged jelly wraps round the other piece
served up suggests the jelly is dished out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letter K is pronounced and spelt out as Kay

explanation.surface: A woman named Kay dishes up jelly outdoors to a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges JELLY to JEYLL, which goes 'outside' K. Dr Jekyll is Stevenson's split-personality doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll is the fictional physician of Stevenson's novella.
